nodes.label: Patient presents with more than 10-year history of dysphagia, with difficulty swallowing dry and heavy-consistency foods
Medical history includes atrial fibrillation, asthma, gastroesophageal reflux disease, Schatzki ring status after multiple dilations, pulmonary hypertension, and hypothyroidism
Patient had multiple esophagogastroduodenoscopies with dilations for Schatzki ring, which provided some relief but did not completely resolve symptoms
Patient denied odynophagia, otalgia, hematemesis, or hemoptysis
Clinical and video swallow evaluation revealed hypertrophy of the cricopharyngeus muscle; during surgery, a palpable thick broad cricopharyngeus muscle was identified
Barium swallow shows cricopharyngeal hypertrophy, thumbprint sign, and cricopharyngeal bar
Postoperative barium study shows the cricopharyngeal bar resolved without leak
Cricopharyngeal biopsy shows endomysial fibrosis, adipose deposition, fiber size variation, internal nuclei, and rare necrotic fibers with negative stains
Cricopharyngeal biopsy shows nonnecrotizing granulomas with negative stains
Manometry, VFSS, and endoscopy reports are unavailable
Available imaging and pathology evaluations show no active mucosal inflammation
Serum ACE, calcium, and chest CT results are pending (sarcoidosis workup not yet completed)
